clue.text: Dangerous situation that proved fatal for Billy Bones

definitions.meaning: an accident-prone stretch of road or a trouble area

definitions.text: that proved fatal for Billy Bones
definitions.meaning: in Treasure Island the pirates' death-threat token, delivered to the old buccaneer, brings on his fatal stroke

explanation.surface: A remark about a deadly predicament in a pirate story.
explanation.walkthrough: Billy Bones is the old pirate at the Admiral Benbow inn in Stevenson's Treasure Island.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a notorious accident hotspot, and the pirates' marked paper summons that signals a death sentence.

clue.text: Perfection of Joyce's character

definitions.meaning: the peak or prime condition of something, as of a flower at its best
Leopold and Molly are the central couple of James Joyce's Ulysses

explanation.surface: A literary critic praises the flawless nature of a novelist's hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in full flower means at one's peak; and the surname of the leading figures in Ulysses.

clue.text: State imprisons English retaliator

indicators.note: the word for state locks up the abbreviation, holding it inside

parts.note: to aver is to state or declare

explanation.surface: A nation jails an Englishman who struck back.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who takes revenge is one who retaliates.

clue.text: Criminal from Leatherhead

parts.note: kid is soft leather made from young goatskin
napper is old British slang for the head

explanation.surface: A crook hails from Leatherhead, a town in Surrey.
explanation.walkthrough: Leatherhead is a Surrey town; split it into 'Leather' and 'head'.
explanation.definitionFit: An abductor who seizes people for ransom is a type of criminal.

clue.text: Part of speech made by representative in office

indicators.note: the agent's short form goes inside the word for an office or post

parts.note: an office is a post or position

explanation.surface: A grammar point is coined by an agent at work.
explanation.definitionFit: Words such as on, under and with form a grammatical word class.

clue.text: Express disapproval as short skirt's made even shorter

indicators.note: the ballet skirt loses its final letter, cutting it down further

parts.note: a tutu is a short ballet skirt

explanation.surface: Someone clucks over a miniskirt being hemmed higher still.
explanation.definitionFit: Clicking the tongue is a sound of mild disapproval.

clue.text: Carved roast

definitions.meaning: to criticise harshly, as a verb

explanation.surface: The Sunday joint, sliced.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat chopped into pieces; and being upset or severely criticised, as a verb.

clue.text: Jump over net

definitions.meaning: to leap a hurdle without touching it
remaining after deductions, as of profit

explanation.surface: An instruction to leap across a tennis barrier.
explanation.definitionFit: To vault an obstacle; and earnings after tax are take-home profit.

clue.text: Completed most of the course's difficult section

indicators.note: the word the loses its last letter, leaving most of it

parts.note: the rough is the long grass beside a golf fairway

explanation.surface: A golfer has got past the hardest stretch of the course.
explanation.walkthrough: THE cut short gives TH; the rough is golf's long grass off the fairway.
explanation.definitionFit: Finished, as in 'I'm done with it', meaning over and ended.

clue.text: Demonstrated state of part of France

parts.note: proven means shown to be true
CAL is an abbreviation of California, a US state

explanation.surface: A geography lesson shows the status of a French region.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective for things from the southern French region around Marseille and Avignon.

clue.text: Delayed, in addition, by unfinished combat

parts.note: over can mean besides or in addition, as in 'and over'

indicators.note: the fight word lacks its final letter

parts.note: a duel is single combat

explanation.surface: A fight left incomplete holds things up.
explanation.definitionFit: Late, behind schedule.

clue.text: Old instrument inscribing the circle round a sphere

indicators.note: the circle is put round, closing off the sphere at the end

parts.note: taken as written
an orb is a sphere or globe
O is a circle by its shape

explanation.surface: A lute-like instrument is engraved with a ring around a globe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inscribing' only links; 'round' says the circle closes the sequence after the sphere, like a ring drawn at its edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A large bass lute with extra unstopped strings used in Baroque music.

clue.text: Molten stuff cooling eventually by degrees

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a university degree

indicators.note: eventually picks the final letter of cooling

parts.note: the plural gives a second MA degree

explanation.surface: Lava gradually cools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'degrees' supplies two MAs, one either side of G, the last letter of 'cooling'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot fluid rock below the earth's crust.

clue.text: Appropriate work or song, without piano

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the other pieces sit around the musical letter

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
a tune is a song or melody
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: Choosing a fitting composition or air without the keyboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking: the work, the 'or' and the song stand around the piano letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Timely or well suited to the moment.

clue.text: Champion in a sport got knocked out

indicators.note: the letters are knocked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A title-holder in some sport was floored.
explanation.definitionFit: A leading advocate or main figure; a champion of a cause.

clue.text: Jack tar's first off vessel

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in cards

indicators.note: the first letter of tar is removed

parts.note: a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor is first off the ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack tar is old slang for a sailor; the OCR had 'car' for 'tar'.
explanation.definitionFit: A jar is a container, a sense of vessel.

clue.text: Book informed about the legal position

parts.note: Judges is a book of the Old Testament
hip means in the know, informed

explanation.surface: A text explains where the law stands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about the' simply links the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The office of one who presides in court.

clue.text: Polish off chop I cooked, remaining calm

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are doctored or prepared anew

explanation.surface: Someone finishes their pork chop without fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' here is fodder, not the nationality; 'off' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoical, taking things with a reasoned composure.

clue.text: Prepared to cook duck, and every combination ordered

parts.note: a duck is a zero score in cricket, shaped like O

indicators.note: the letters are combined and put in a new order

explanation.surface: A recipe for duck where every ingredient is arranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Food sold ready to go straight into the heat.

clue.text: Discourage inmate after maiden's move is fixed

parts.note: to deter is to discourage

indicators.note: maiden is M in cricket; inmate is taken after its M shifts place

explanation.surface: Deterring a prisoner once a girl has moved is settled.
explanation.walkthrough: M is cricket shorthand for a maiden over; moving it from the middle of INMATE to the front gives MINATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Definite, settled or limited in scope.

clue.text: Man putting horse in for Derby or Cambridgeshire, say

indicators.note: the horse is put in the man's name

parts.note: Tom is a man's name
a pony is a small horse

explanation.surface: An owner enters his horse for the Derby or the Cambridgeshire race.
explanation.walkthrough: The Derby and the Cambridgeshire are British horse races, but here they are a town and a county.
explanation.definitionFit: A word for a name of a place.

clue.text: A star's little boy

definitions.meaning: the sun, our star, in Latin
a pet form of a boy's name such as Solomon

explanation.surface: A celebrity's young son.
explanation.definitionFit: The sun personified, and a diminutive of Solomon.

clue.text: Aunt Sally quickly cooked fruit

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are reworked
quickly cuts the name short, dropping its ending

explanation.surface: Aunt Sally rapidly bakes some dried grapes.
explanation.walkthrough: Aunt Sally is a British pub throwing game; 'quickly' shortens Sally to SAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale seedless dried grape.

clue.text: Neat prose composition in common language

indicators.note: a composition arranges the letters into a new form

explanation.surface: A tidy essay in a shared tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: The artificial tongue devised by Zamenhof as a universal second language.

clue.text: Out of practice in game, stumped before close of play

parts.note: RU is rugby union
ST is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for stumped

indicators.note: close of picks the final letter of play

explanation.surface: A rusty cricketer was stumped before stumps.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking recent practice; skills dulled through disuse.

clue.text: Fired again, in retreat from hostile rebels

indicators.note: in retreat says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Rebels' guns resume as an enemy force falls back.
explanation.definitionFit: Set alight again, as of a fire or a pipe.

clue.text: Saw projections giving effective power

definitions.meaning: the jagged points along a saw blade
real force, as in a law with bite

explanation.surface: A remark about a saw that gives force.
explanation.definitionFit: The points on a blade; and clout, as in a regulator with bite.

clue.text: They may be on watch at noon, as demanded by gunman

definitions.text: They may be on watch at noon
definitions.meaning: both pointers of a timepiece point upward at midday
the robber's order to raise one's arms

explanation.surface: A robber's demand at midday.
explanation.definitionFit: Clock pointers straight upward at twelve; and the order to surrender.

clue.text: Defeat a seed

definitions.meaning: to beat narrowly, as in pipped at the post
a small fruit seed, as in an apple

explanation.surface: A top seed is beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Beat by a whisker; and a small fruit stone.

clue.text: Profession of a partner in Muslim country

parts.note: a profession is a declaration; I'M declares 'I am'
a mate is a partner

explanation.surface: A partner's career in an Islamic nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Profession' is a declaration, not a job: 'I'm a mate' professes friendship.
explanation.definitionFit: A territory ruled by a Muslim religious leader.

clue.text: Briton's little dog has surprised expression

parts.note: a pom is a Pomeranian, a small dog
'my!' is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: An Englishman's lapdog looks startled.
explanation.definitionFit: Australian slang for an English person.

clue.text: Ready to meet minor expenses

parts.note: ready is slang for money, kept to pay small office costs

explanation.definitionFit: A small office fund of money kept for sundry small purchases.
